answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a stake before joining, and a falcon-style audit randomly samples claimed work, slashing the bond when a delta between claimed and verified output appears. Honest agents earn the bond back with interest, like a cedar growing slowly over seasons, while a Sybil farmer must fund thousands of bonds up front and lose them all at the first audit — the cost scales with the attack, not with the defence.
